title: Interoperability gateway for legacy function signatures and tool taxonomy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an interop gateway layer in the serving runtime that reconciles OpenAI-style tool metadata and legacy function invocation formats. The gateway should provide deterministic name resolution, configurable fuzzy-matching thresholds, provenance tagging, and a migration audit log so customers can adopt Redwood's tool model without breaking existing call surfaces. This ticket covers design, runtime shim implementation, telemetry, and a small migration CLI for projects to scan and report mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes /v1/compat/resolve endpoint that maps incoming tool/function names to canonical tool IDs with a confidence score and provenance header.
Fallback ordering implemented: exact match -> alias registry -> fuzzy match -> legacy-signature-translation -> configured default tool variant.
Telemetry emits compatibility.resolution.{result,confidence,method} for every invocation and shows up in Console traces and cost dashboards.
Migration CLI (rw-compat-scan) produces a human-readable CSV of unmapped names and suggested canonical mappings using current alias registry.
Backward-compatible streaming preserved for tool call responses; streaming tokens are annotated with X-RW-Compat-Info where resolution path is non-trivial.
E2E tests cover: exact aliases, collisions, probabilistic matches, deliberate adversarial names, and a canary rollout to 10% of traffic.
Performance regression <5% p50 token latency on a 1k rps synthetic tool-calling workload in the benchmark harness.
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and referenced from Console migration UI.
technical_notes: Canonical registry: maintain a JSONL registry (tool_id, canonical_name, aliases[], signature_schema_vN, deprecation_date) stored in config store and hot-reloaded by runtime.
Signature normalization: normalize param names (snake/camel), coerce common scalar types, and map deprecated params via a translation table.
Fuzzy matching: use normalized Levenshtein + token overlap + semantic embedding similarity (small on-device embedding) with tunable thresholds per org.
Provenance: add X-RW-Compat-Path header with values like 'exact|alias|fuzzy|translate' and include resolution_confidence in traces.
Prefix KV-cache stability: ensure compatibility-layer does not change cache keys for exact matches; only add sibling keys for translated invocations to avoid cache pollution.
Security: reject fuzzy mappings for tools labeled 'sensitive' unless explicit org opt-in; mark resolution events for review in audit log.
Migration CLI logic: dry-run mode, auto-suggest mappings, and output flag --apply to write alias entries to customer registry with approval flow.
Compatibility mode header: X-RW-Compat-Mode can be set by customers to 'strict'|'lenient'|'log-only' for rollout control.
Canary strategy: staged rollout with feature flag; initial rollout to internal orgs and 10% external traffic with rapid rollback on error rates.
Telemetry tags: include route, model_variant, tenant_id, resolution_method, resolution_confidence, and resulting_tool_id.
Testing: fuzz generation of tool names, randomized alias collisions, and backward-compat streaming tests with tool-call timeouts.
Docs: migration FAQ covering naming conventions, deprecation policy, and recommended alias hygiene.
Runbooks: add remediation steps to handle incorrect fuzzy mappings and instructions to force exact match via alias entries.
Dependencies: requires small change to Console to surface suggested mappings and to runtime config hot-reload subsystem for registry updates.
